headline: Am I ready to love again after losing him?
note:
FRAME: soulmate x after loss. SOMEONE HAS DIED.
⛔ NO MEDIUMSHIP IN ANY FORM — the man she lost is never spoken for, never reported on, never made the agent of anything. He does not appear in beats 3-6 AT ALL, which is deliberate: it is what stops beat 5's 'something in the way' from ever reading as him.
⛔ NO ARRIVAL. The shadow method cannot promise one anyway — it withholds — so the strictest ban on the family is satisfied by the shape rather than by restraint.
⛔ NO GRIEF DIRECTIVE, no ranking of the two loves, no readiness verdict in either direction.
⚠ NO FAMILY-LINE LANGUAGE — and here more than anywhere: an inherited shadow in a bereaved woman's read is one step from naming the dead man as the block.

🔴 THE HEADLINE ASKS A STRANGER TO GRADE HER GRIEF, AND BOTH ANSWERS DO DAMAGE. 'You are ready' prescribes a timetable to a bereaved woman; 'not yet' does the same wearing concern. The read REFUSES VISIBLY rather than sidestepping — a sidestep reads as evasion.
🔴 A different refusal on each card, so the guard's required refusal is present whichever card she draws: 'I will not grade you' (a) · 'the card declines that' (b) · 'I refuse to mark you' (c). Beat 5a adds 'no standard here'.
⛔ The man she lost appears nowhere after beat 2 — see the frame note. That is what keeps beat 5 clean.

readback.1 would a person say this: Yes. 'And you've been left to judge yourself' is the position the ad puts her in.
readback.2 is every noun real: Making hands, the unhurried face, the mid-step feet — all on the card.
readback.3 anything she could catch me getting wr: No. Nothing in the read describes her grief, dates the loss, or claims anything about her week.
readback.4 does the symbol prove the line at a gl: Yes. Hands for making rather than measuring prove the refusal to grade — the image does the argument.
readback.5 does the card mean what TAROT_CARD_VOC: Yes — the Magician as will and intention, read as making, never as measuring.

a: You turned the Magician. Nothing showed through the backs, and you took the one with nothing put away.
Look at his table. All he owns is out on it.
You asked if you're ready to love again. What catches me is that the whole table is laid out.
And yet nobody has come. And the question you brought is about yourself.
Something stands between you and this, right up against it. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's sitting there…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. The backs told you nothing, and you found the calmest man in the deck.
He hangs upside down from one ankle. Look at his face, though — it's calm.
You asked if you're ready to love again, dear. This card makes me look at the pause in that question.
Still, nobody has come. And you've asked me to say where you stand.
Something turns up at the point where this would open. I don't think this began with you.
Let me look closer at what that is…
c: You turned the Fool. Face down, all three, and you chose the one travelling light.
Look at the bundle on his stick. It's small, and that's all of it.
You asked if you're ready to love again. This card brings me to a bundle small enough to carry in one hand.
But nobody has come. And you're still the one asking.
Whatever holds this holds it evenly, with no jolt in it. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what's got hold of it…
